criteria: Are the subject, mission and reference roles distinct and internally consistent throughout R1 through R10 and the acceptance fixtures?

Can the proposed logical selectors, request identities, Review Intent identities and packet identities distinguish materially different requests without ambiguity, including mutable remote references, inline content, uploaded bytes and cross-version predecessors?

Can a mutable reference change between two executions or during preparation without the proposed identity rules causing a silent snapshot substitution, inconsistent reconstruction or unauthorized second model invocation?
Do the proposed pre-PREPARED and post-PREPARED recovery rules establish a coherent durable commitment boundary and preserve at-most-once invocation even when acquisition or evidence recovery fails?
Does the proposal maintain exact GitHub PR changed-file scope independently of reference material, including omitted references and citation source identities?
Can required versus optional reference handling produce a false completeness claim, conceal unauthorized source access or allow unverified provenance assertions to become trusted facts?
Are the distinctions between received bytes, source-authenticated provenance, technical evidence validation, substantive reviewer conclusions and downstream consumer authority internally consistent?
Can reference applicability change independently of subject applicability without mutating a historical ReviewResult or claiming that unobserved sources remain current?

Does the proposed successor contract preserve historical v1/v2 identities and distinguish requester-owned semantic mission choices from broker-owned runtime permissions without internally contradictory obligations?

Are the proposed source kinds, acquisition stages, identifiers, statuses, freshness rules and security controls necessary for the stated product requirement, or does the document introduce unjustified abstractions or implementation commitments?
Are GitHub PR references, uploaded files, external URLs, HTML documents and PDFs explicitly bounded as future acquisition forms rather than falsely claimed implemented functionality?
Are material claims requiring absent Issues #43/#44/#51, existing source code or governing contracts explicitly left unverified rather than asserted as independently established?
mission.instructions: Examine only the exact source snapshots and PR diff supplied in the immutable packet. Treat the proposal as non-normative and unaccepted. Seek concrete counterexamples, internal contradictions, missing obligations, ambiguous definitions, unsafe assumptions and unjustified compatibility claims. Challenge every material claim that can be examined from the packet. Do not assume access to Issues #43, #44 or #51, governing contracts, schemas or implementation files unless their exact contents are present in the packet. Do not treat references to those documents as verified evidence. Clearly report unavailable cross-document verification and other residual uncertainties. Cite exact source IDs and physical lines for findings. Never manufacture a favorable verdict. A GO is not product-owner acceptance, normative contract adoption, implementation authorization or proof of Review Broker construction security.
mission.objective: Independently falsify the internal coherence, identity semantics, recovery guarantees, reference provenance and minimality of the non-normative requester-declared reference contract proposal in PR #52, strictly within the exact changed material provided by Review Broker.
